templates.pattern: A wave has a frequency of [F] Hz and a wavelength of [L] m. Calculate the wave speed in m/s.
templates.explanation:
Wave speed = frequency × wavelength
= v = fλ
= [F] × [L]
= [RESULT] m/s

This equation applies to all types of waves including sound, light and water waves.

templates.pattern: A wave travels at [V] m/s and has a wavelength of [L] m. Calculate the frequency of the wave in Hz.
templates.explanation:
Frequency = wave speed ÷ wavelength
= f = v ÷ λ
= [V] ÷ [L]
= [RESULT] Hz

Frequency tells us how many complete waves pass a fixed point every second.

templates.pattern: A wave has a speed of [V] m/s and a frequency of [F] Hz. Calculate the wavelength of the wave in metres.
templates.explanation:
Wavelength = wave speed ÷ frequency
= λ = v ÷ f
= [V] ÷ [F]
= [RESULT] m

Wavelength is the distance between two successive crests or two successive troughs of a wave.

templates.pattern: A sound wave travels [D] m through air in [T] seconds. Calculate the speed of sound in m/s.
templates.explanation:
Speed of sound = Distance ÷ Time
= [D] ÷ [T]
= [RESULT] m/s

The speed of sound in air is approximately 340 m/s at room temperature. It is much faster in liquids and solids.

templates.pattern: A source produces [N] complete wave oscillations in [T] seconds. Calculate the frequency of the wave in Hz.
templates.explanation:
Frequency = number of oscillations ÷ time
= f = N ÷ t
= [N] ÷ [T]
= [RESULT] Hz

Frequency is measured in hertz (Hz). 1 Hz means one complete oscillation per second.

templates.pattern: A wave has a frequency of [F] Hz. Calculate the time period of the wave in seconds.
templates.explanation:
Time period = 1 ÷ frequency
= T = 1 ÷ f
= 1 ÷ [F]
= [RESULT] s

The time period is the time taken for one complete oscillation. Period and frequency are reciprocals of each other.

templates.pattern: A person shouts near a cliff and hears the echo after [T] seconds. The speed of sound is [V] m/s. Calculate the distance from the person to the cliff in metres.
templates.explanation:
The sound travels to the cliff and back — so total distance = v × t
Distance to cliff = v × t ÷ 2
= [V] × [T] ÷ 2
= [V*T] ÷ 2
= [RESULT] m

This is the principle used in SONAR and echo location.

templates.pattern: Ultrasound of frequency [F] kHz travels at [V] m/s through soft tissue. Calculate the wavelength of the ultrasound in the tissue in millimetres.
templates.explanation:
Wavelength = speed ÷ frequency
= [V] ÷ ([F] × 1000)
= [V] ÷ [F*1000] m
= [RESULT] mm

Ultrasound uses frequencies above 20,000 Hz. Shorter wavelengths give better resolution in medical imaging.

templates.pattern: A water wave has a wavelength of [L] m and a time period of [T] seconds. Calculate the speed of the wave in m/s.
templates.explanation:
Wave speed = wavelength ÷ period
= v = λ ÷ T
= [L] ÷ [T]
= [RESULT] m/s

This is equivalent to v = fλ since f = 1/T. The period tells us how long each wave takes to pass a fixed point.

templates.pattern: A sound wave travels at [V] m/s through air and has a wavelength of [L] cm. Calculate the frequency of the sound in Hz.
templates.explanation:
Convert wavelength to metres: [L] cm = [L/100] m
Frequency = speed ÷ wavelength
= [V] ÷ [L/100]
= [RESULT] Hz

Human hearing range is approximately 20 Hz to 20,000 Hz. Sound waves in this range have wavelengths from about 17 mm to 17 m.
